subject: Using Stan for large simulation (repeated calling)

messages.author: afc5d1777b0456fc
messages.subject: Using Stan for large simulation (repeated calling)
parts:
Dear all,

I am new to stan, and is planning to use rstan to run simulations to compare the performance of different models, including a Bayesian hierarchical model.

My question is: I'm going to call the same *.stan file 1,000 times for different simulated data, is there a way to only call the C++ translation once to save time?

sample code:

for (i in 1:1000){
  dat <- data[[i]]
  m2 <- stan(file="model.stan", data=dat,iter=100000, chains=1,thin=10)
  var[i]<-1-mean(m2@sim$samples[[1]]$var)
  }



Thanks in advance,
Craig

MSc in Statistics at ETH

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Using Stan for large simulation (repeated calling)
parts:
On Thursday, November 26, 2015 at 8:42:27 AM UTC-5, Craig Wang wrote:
My question is: I'm going to call the same *.stan file 1,000 times for different simulated data, is there a way to only call the C++ translation once to save time?

Yes, in RStan and PyStan. In RStan, it should not compile the same model repeatedly within the same R session, but you can have it not compile repeatedly across R sessions by first calling

rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)

In both RStan and PyStan, you can pass an existing object produced by stan() to the fit argument of stan() to use the same model with different data.

sample code:

for (i in 1:1000){
  dat <- data[[i]]
  m2 <- stan(file="model.stan", data=dat,iter=100000, chains=1,thin=10)
  var[i]<-1-mean(m2@sim$samples[[1]]$var)
  }

With Stan, we do not recommend doing 100000 iterations, one chain, or thinning like you might do with a Gibbs sampler or Metropolis-Hastings. The default arguments are more than fine the vast majority of the time. You should read about the differences between how Stan does MCMC relative to a Gibbs sampler or Metropolis-Hastings before doing a bunch of simulations. Also, we do not recommend using syntax like @sim$samples[[1]]$. Use mean(extract(m2, pars = "var", permuted = FALSE)) or something.

Ben
